subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to follow symlinks from the workspace into sibling `~/.openclaw` directories, and what roots must remain blocked?
rationale: The failure is source-reproducible, but the fix changes which local filesystem roots can feed automatic startup prompt context, so automation cannot choose the permanent trust boundary safely.

options.title: Allow narrow bootstrap-only symlinks
options.body: Permit only fixed top-level bootstrap symlinks to readable regular files under an explicit safe-root policy while blocking private OpenClaw state, credential, session, cache, log, non-regular, dangling, oversized, and hardlinked targets.

options.title: Keep strict boundary with diagnostics
options.body: Continue rejecting out-of-workspace symlink targets but render a boundary-blocked diagnostic so users can distinguish policy blocks from missing files.

options.title: Allow broad `.openclaw` sibling targets
options.body: Treat the whole user `~/.openclaw` tree as trusted for this bootstrap path, accepting a wider prompt-context authority boundary that needs explicit security ownership.

recommendation.title: Allow narrow bootstrap-only symlinks
recommendation.body: Permit only fixed top-level bootstrap symlinks to readable regular files under an explicit safe-root policy while blocking private OpenClaw state, credential, session, cache, log, non-regular, dangling, oversized, and hardlinked targets.

likelyOwner.reason: He commented to keep this issue open and owns the active maintainer-labeled replacement path for overlapping bootstrap symlink behavior.
